Boundary: 2019 includes former Goldcorp sites (Peñasquito, Red Lake, Porcupine, Éléonore, Musselwhite, Cerro Negro; acquired 18 April 2019) and KCGM, and excludes Nevada (contributed to Nevada Gold Mines JV operated by Barrick from 1 July 2019). 2015-2018 trailing data are NOT restated to the 2019 portfolio (footnote A187: adjusting 2018 would reduce consumption by 12,979 ML, increase recycling by 13,970 ML and raise % recycled from 68% to 71%).

2015 figures include Batu Hijau (Indonesia, divested 2016): withdrawal 503029 ML incl. 209048 ML ocean cooling water and 62687 ML ocean process water, and 209048 ML untreated discharge to ocean. Withdrawal fell to 201152 ML in 2016.

Trend (as reported, unadjusted): withdrawal 201152 (2016) -> 217327 (2017) -> 230257 (2018) -> 198549 ML (2019); consumption (GRI) 104816 -> 106413 ML 2018->2019; recycling 263210 ML, 71% of water used. Intensity 19 -> 16.8 kL/GEO 2015->2019.

Consumption: site/corporate 'Total water consumed' is the GRI definition (withdrawn minus discharged). The ICMM-definition consumption (evaporation + entrainment + other) for 2019 is 177,390 ML (footnote A187), 67% higher; recorded as other:consumption_icmm.

Internal inconsistency: total discharge = 92136 ML in the site summary (D26) and water balance (B178), but the category table total is 92043 ML (J53). The gap comes from CC&V (111 ML in D8 vs 0 in J35) and Cerro Negro (0 in D17 vs 18 in J44). Category consumption (B164:B166) therefore sums to 106,506 ML vs 106,413 ML reported, and percentages sum to 101%.

Internal inconsistency: 2019 water balance reports groundwater discharge 4441 ML (B180) and surface 87695 ML, but the untreated table shows 4632 ML untreated discharge to groundwater (KCGM, D103) and Akyem/Peñasquito groundwater reinjection is included in 'treated by other'.

Internal inconsistency: 2016 consumption is 107586 ML in row 142 but 107585 ML in row 184 (both recorded). Also 2018 'Total environmental releases' (Spills and Releases E6) is 0 although on-site releases were 50. Site withdrawal_total values sum to 198,548 ML vs 198,549 total (rounding).

Footnote A27 states 'Reported Newmont-only sites in 2019 included withdrawal - 230.3ML, discharge - 125.4ML' which does not match any table value (likely a units/typo error). Former Goldcorp sites did not report by quality category and their discharge-type breakout is omitted (their total 2019 discharge was 10,736 ML per footnote A80); category tables for those sites appear to be estimated.

Water intensity figures are consumption-based (kL consumed per GEO / per tonne ore); intensity per tonne ore and per revenue were first reported in 2019 (N/R before). The per-revenue figure (0.12 'kL / billions revenues') is implausibly small as labelled.

Water stress (site table rows 196-210): baseline water stress risk flagged (WBCSD/WRI Aqueduct) at KCGM, Tanami, CC&V, Peñasquito and Cerro Negro; no withdrawal volume in water-stressed areas is disclosed. Excess-water risk at Ahafo, Akyem, Éléonore, Red Lake, Merian, Yanacocha.

Merian (Suriname) and Yanacocha (Peru) are dominated by precipitation capture (36,834 and 35,448 ML) and discharge large volumes (37,000 and 34,087 ML); Peñasquito is 93% groundwater (26,374 ML) in an arid water-stressed setting with the highest consumption (28,107 ML) and a 111-day trucking contractor/community blockade in 2019 (Compliance D30; disclosure cross-references the water stewardship section). Yanacocha: Nov 2019 community protest over turbidity in China Linda spring (Compliance C25).

Fines (Compliance sheet): 2019 environmental/social fines totalled USD 169864, incl. Peñasquito USD 16,751 for tailings dam seepage (2017 event) and three Yanacocha cyanide-solution spill fines (2017 events, one reaching Yanacocha creek). Not recorded as water_fines_usd because the file does not classify them as water fines.
Spills and Releases: 2019 total environmental releases 650 (647 on site) vs 50 in 2018 - likely reflects Goldcorp integration/reporting-system change; cyanide releases 4,745 kL in 2019.
No ore processed or gold production figures are disclosed in this workbook (intensity denominators only).
